concepts.definition: Epithet of Poseidon, referring to his power to cause earthquakes.

concepts.name: Trident
concepts.definition: Three-pronged fork, symbol and weapon of Poseidon.

concepts.name: Palladium
concepts.definition: A wooden image of Pallas, decked with the aegis, that fell to Troy and was tied to the city's destiny.

concepts.name: Panathenaic amphora
concepts.definition: Prize amphora filled with oil, depicting Athena in war gear, awarded at the Panathenaic games.

concepts.name: Peplos
concepts.definition: Ceremonial robe presented to the priestess of Athena during the Panathenaea.

concepts.name: Elgin marbles
concepts.definition: Major fragments of the Parthenon pediments and friezes housed in the British Museum.

concepts.name: arete
concepts.definition: Excellence or virtue, especially in the context of a woman's skill in weaving or a man's in war.

concepts.name: glaukopis
concepts.definition: Homeric epithet for Athena meaning 'gray-eyed' or 'owl-eyed'.

concepts.name: Vienna Secession
concepts.definition: Art movement in late 19th-century Vienna that sought to break from traditional art forms.

concepts.name: Panathenaic Festival
concepts.definition: Festival in Athens honoring Athena, with contests and prizes.

concepts.name: Aphrodite Urania
concepts.definition: Celestial Aphrodite, sprung from Uranus alone; represents ethereal, spiritual love.

concepts.name: Aphrodite Pandemos
concepts.definition: Common Aphrodite, sprung from Zeus and Dione; represents physical, profane love.

concepts.name: Sacred vs Profane Love
concepts.definition: Distinction between spiritual (Urania) and physical (Pandemos) love; a profound archetype.

concepts.name: Temple Prostitution
concepts.definition: Practice of temple harlots in honor of Aphrodite; evidence lacking for widespread occurrence.

concepts.name: Great Mother
concepts.definition: Archetypal mother goddess whose lover dies and is reborn, representing vegetation cycles.

concepts.name: Pre-Raphaelite
concepts.definition: 19th-century artistic movement rejecting academic conventions, drawing on myth and legend.

concepts.name: ambrosial oil
concepts.definition: Oil used by the gods, perfumed with heavenly sweetness.

concepts.name: androgynous
concepts.definition: Original third sex in Aristophanes' speech, partaking of both male and female characteristics.

concepts.name: Love as desire for wholeness
concepts.definition: In Aristophanes' speech, love is the desire and pursuit of one's other half, aiming to restore the original unified nature of humans.

concepts.name: Eros as a great spirit
concepts.definition: In Socrates' speech, Eros is described as a daimon, intermediate between god and human, interpreting and conveying exchanges between them.

concepts.name: Platonic Eros
concepts.definition: A philosophical love that inspires the pursuit of wisdom and beauty, transcending physical desire; a love of the eternal and immortal.

concepts.name: Symposium
concepts.definition: A Platonic dialogue in which Socrates and others discuss the nature of love.

concepts.name: Metamorphoses (The Golden Ass)
concepts.definition: A novel by Apuleius containing the story of Cupid and Psyche.

concepts.name: lesbian
concepts.definition: Term derived from Sappho's association with Lesbos, referring to female same-sex love.

concepts.name: Arcteia
concepts.definition: Rite performed at Brauron where girls 'played the bear' for Artemis as an initiation before marriage.

concepts.name: Potnia Theron
concepts.definition: Title meaning 'Mistress of Animals,' used for Artemis.

concepts.name: misogyny
concepts.definition: Hatred of women, exemplified by Hippolytus' tirade against women.

concepts.name: misandry
concepts.definition: Hatred of men, associated with Artemis and the Amazons.

concepts.name: sophrosyne
concepts.definition: Greek concept meaning good sense, self-control, and moderation; translated as 'to be temperate' in the text.

concepts.name: deus ex machina
concepts.definition: A god appearing by machine to resolve the plot; Artemis appears as such in the play.

concepts.name: Mysteries
concepts.definition: Religious rites, possibly the Eleusinian Mysteries; Phaedra saw Hippolytus participating in them.

concepts.name: Curse of Poseidon
concepts.definition: A curse granted by Poseidon to Theseus, which Theseus used to cause Hippolytus' death.

concepts.name: Rites of Hippolytus
concepts.definition: Honors bestowed by Artemis on Hippolytus in Troezen, where unmarried girls cut their hair in dedication before marriage.

concepts.name: Initiation rites
concepts.definition: Rituals for girls' transition to adulthood, often associated with Artemis, such as the 'Bear and Fawn' rites.

concepts.name: Homeric Hymn to Apollo
concepts.definition: A hymn in the Homeric tradition that narrates the birth of Apollo and his establishment at Delos and Delphi.

concepts.name: Deliades
concepts.definition: Maidens who serve Apollo at Delos, known for their singing and ability to imitate dialects.

concepts.name: omphalos
concepts.definition: An archaic stone shaped like an egg, kept in the temple at Delphi, signifying that Delphi was the center of the earth.

concepts.name: Pythian Games
concepts.definition: Festival held every four years at Delphi, including athletic and intellectual competitions; second only to the Olympic Games.

concepts.name: tripod
concepts.definition: A three-legged bowl used as a seat for the Pythia during prophecy; symbol of Apollo's prophetic power.

concepts.name: adyton
concepts.definition: The inner sanctuary of the temple at Delphi where the Pythia prophesied, containing the omphalos.

concepts.name: Pythia
concepts.definition: The title of the priestess of Apollo at Delphi who delivered oracles, often while inhaling narcotic vapors.

concepts.name: Sibyl
concepts.definition: A generic term for a prophetess; many Sibyls existed in the ancient world, with the Cumaean Sibyl being among the most famous.

concepts.name: Sibylline books
concepts.definition: Collections of prophecies of the Sibyls, often consulted by the Romans.

concepts.name: Hyacinthia
concepts.definition: Annual festival in honor of Hyacinthus, celebrated in Sparta with ancient traditions.

concepts.name: incubation
concepts.definition: Practice of sleeping in a sanctuary to receive divine healing or dreams, associated with Asclepius and Amphiaraüs.

concepts.name: staff of Asclepius
concepts.definition: Symbol of the medical profession: a staff entwined by a single serpent, representing rejuvenation and healing.

concepts.name: caduceus
concepts.definition: Winged staff of Hermes with two coiled serpents, symbol of commerce and messengers; sometimes confused with the staff of Asclepius in medical symbolism.

concepts.name: Asclepiadae
concepts.definition: Guild of physicians who considered themselves spiritual children of Asclepius.

concepts.name: Apollonian
concepts.definition: Relating to Apollo, representing rational, disciplined, and intellectual aspects of human psychology and culture.

concepts.name: Dionysiac
concepts.definition: Relating to Dionysus, representing irrational, mystical, and ecstatic forces.

concepts.name: Know thyself
concepts.definition: Proverbial Greek maxim associated with Apollo, advocating self-knowledge.

concepts.name: Nothing too much
concepts.definition: Proverbial Greek maxim associated with Apollo, advocating moderation.

concepts.name: Pythian
concepts.definition: Title of Apollo derived from Pytho, the place where he slew the she-dragon.

concepts.name: Telphusian
concepts.definition: Title of Apollo derived from Telphusa, the spring he shamed.

concepts.name: Ie Paean
concepts.definition: A title of Apollo, associated with healing and victory hymns.

concepts.name: Delphinius
concepts.definition: Epithet of Apollo meaning 'dolphin,' derived from his appearance as a dolphin when he first leaped aboard the Cretan ship.

concepts.name: Stepteria
concepts.definition: Festival celebrated every ninth year at Delphi commemorating Apollo's slaying of Python.

concepts.name: Sortes Vergilianae
concepts.definition: Practice of using Vergil's works as oracles.

concepts.name: Asclepius staff
concepts.definition: Staff with a serpent entwined; symbol of medicine, associated with Asclepius.

concepts.name: Panhellenic festivals
concepts.definition: Major religious festivals attended by all Greeks; included Olympian, Nemean, Isthmian, and Pythian Games.

concepts.name: Homeric Hymn to Hermes
concepts.definition: A hymn that tells the story of Hermes' birth and childhood, including the invention of the lyre and theft of Apollo's cattle.

concepts.name: lyre
concepts.definition: A stringed musical instrument invented by Hermes from a tortoise shell.

concepts.name: fire sticks
concepts.definition: A device for producing fire, invented by Hermes.

concepts.name: asphodel meadow
concepts.definition: A meadow associated with the underworld, mentioned in the context of cattle tracks.

concepts.name: nectar and ambrosia
concepts.definition: Food and drink of the gods, stored in Maia's cave.

concepts.name: pipes
concepts.definition: A wind instrument invented by Hermes, producing sound heard from afar.

concepts.name: petasus
concepts.definition: A wide-brimmed hat worn by Hermes, associated with travel.

concepts.name: winged boots
concepts.definition: Sandals with wings worn by Hermes, enabling swift travel.

concepts.name: divination
concepts.definition: The practice of seeking knowledge of the future or the unknown, often through oracles or omens. Apollo and the holy sisters are masters of divination.

concepts.name: oath of the gods
concepts.definition: A solemn oath sworn by the gods, often by the river Styx, considered binding.

concepts.name: herm
concepts.definition: Square pillar with male genitals and head of Hermes, used as boundary marker and fertility symbol.

concepts.name: psychopompos
concepts.definition: Guide of souls to the Underworld, a function of Hermes.

concepts.name: talaria
concepts.definition: Winged sandals worn by Hermes.

concepts.name: Hermetica
concepts.definition: Corpus of works attributed to Hermes Trismegistus, dealing with philosophy, astrology, and alchemy.

concepts.name: Hermaphrodite
concepts.definition: A being with both male and female characteristics, as exemplified by Hermaphroditus after his merger with Salmacis.

concepts.name: Herms
concepts.definition: Stone pillars with a head of Hermes and male genitals, used as boundary markers; their mutilation was a scandal in Athens.

concepts.name: Thriae
concepts.definition: Eponymous nymphs of divining pebbles, described as women with wings and hair powdered with white flour.

concepts.name: Panpipes
concepts.definition: Shepherds' pipes of reed, also called panpipes, said to be invented by the god Pan.

concepts.name: Bacchic mysteries
concepts.definition: Rituals and teachings associated with the worship of Dionysus, involving ecstatic dance and spiritual revelation.

concepts.name: thyrsus
concepts.definition: An ivy-covered staff carried by Dionysus and his followers, symbolizing his power.

concepts.name: maenad
concepts.definition: Female follower of Dionysus, often depicted in ecstatic frenzy.

concepts.name: satyr
concepts.definition: Male companion of Dionysus, often depicted as half-human, half-goat.

concepts.name: sileni
concepts.definition: Older satyrs, companions of Dionysus.

concepts.name: kantharos
concepts.definition: A wine cup associated with Dionysus.

concepts.name: Maenadism
concepts.definition: Frenzied female worship of Dionysus, characterized by wild dancing, hunting, and raw flesh consumption.

concepts.name: Sparagmos
concepts.definition: The ritual tearing apart of a victim, such as the goat or Pentheus, in Bacchic rites.

concepts.name: Omophagia
concepts.definition: The eating of raw flesh in Bacchic rituals.

concepts.name: Bacchic rites
concepts.definition: Rituals of Dionysus (Bacchus) involving ecstatic dancing, wine, and possession; often performed by women (maenads) in the mountains at night.

concepts.name: Maenads
concepts.definition: Female followers of Dionysus, also called Bacchae, who engage in ecstatic worship.

concepts.name: Omophagy
concepts.definition: The eating of raw flesh in Dionysiac ritual, a kind of ritual communion since the god was believed to be present in the victim.

concepts.name: Thiasus
concepts.definition: The religious congregation of Dionysiac worship, divided into groups often with a male leader playing the role of the god.

concepts.name: Satyrs
concepts.definition: Male companions of Dionysus, part man and part animal (horse or goat attributes); they dance, sing, love music, make wine, and chase maenads.

concepts.name: Agriania
concepts.definition: A festival involving a ritual pursuit of women by night and a return to normal order the next day; connected with the myth of the daughters of Proetus.

concepts.name: resurrection-god
concepts.definition: A god who dies and is reborn; Dionysus is described as such.

concepts.name: panic
concepts.definition: Madness spread by Pan among shepherds.

concepts.name: Echo
concepts.definition: A nymph who could only repeat the last words spoken; also the phenomenon of sound reflection.

concepts.name: Self-knowledge
concepts.definition: The concept that knowing oneself can be dangerous, as in Tiresias' prophecy for Narcissus.

concepts.name: Narcissism
concepts.definition: A psychological term for self-love and self-destruction, derived from the myth of Narcissus.

concepts.name: Homeric Hymn to Demeter
concepts.definition: A lengthy ancient Greek hymn that narrates the myth of Demeter and Persephone, including the abduction and Demeter's stay at Eleusis.

concepts.name: River Styx
concepts.definition: River in the underworld, by which the gods swear unbreakable oaths.

concepts.name: Kore
concepts.definition: Greek word meaning 'girl,' used as an epithet for Persephone.

concepts.name: Lesser Mysteries
concepts.definition: Preliminary initiation stage held in Athens in early spring, focusing on purification.

concepts.name: Greater Mysteries
concepts.definition: Full initiation stage held annually in September-October, involving processions, sacrifices, and secret rites at Eleusis.

concepts.name: Hiera
concepts.definition: Sacred objects revealed by the Hierophant during the highest rites of the mysteries.

concepts.name: Hierophant
concepts.definition: High priest who revealed the Hiera to initiates; title means 'he who reveals the Hiera.'

concepts.name: Kykeon
concepts.definition: Sacred drink consumed by initiates during the mysteries, possibly ending a fast.

concepts.name: Kernos
concepts.definition: Sacred vessel for offerings used in the rites of Eleusis.

concepts.name: Kernophoria
concepts.definition: Bearing of the kernoi, part of the Greater and Lesser Mysteries.

concepts.name: Pannychis
concepts.definition: Nighttime celebration following the arrival of initiates in Eleusis.

concepts.name: Bacchoi
concepts.definition: Sacred wands carried in the torch-lit procession to Eleusis.

concepts.name: Anaktoron
concepts.definition: Enclosed structure within the Telesterion at Eleusis, possibly containing sacred objects.

concepts.name: Telesterion
concepts.definition: Temple of Demeter at Eleusis where the final revelation of the mysteries was celebrated.

concepts.name: Pelanos
concepts.definition: Sacred cake offering of barley and wheat, possibly depicted on the Niinnion Pinax.

concepts.name: Kiste
concepts.definition: Covered basket symbolizing secrecy in the ritual, possibly depicted on the Niinnion Pinax.

concepts.name: Orphism
concepts.definition: Religious movement based on the myth of Zagreus-Dionysus, emphasizing immortality and redemption.

concepts.name: Mystery religion
concepts.definition: Religious cult with secret rites and promises of afterlife benefits, such as the Eleusinian Mysteries.

concepts.name: Epopteia
concepts.definition: The highest stage of initiation in the Eleusinian Mysteries, involving further revelation.

concepts.name: Eumolpids
concepts.definition: Priestly family at Eleusis, descended from Eumolpus.

concepts.name: Kerykes
concepts.definition: Priestly family at Eleusis.

concepts.name: Mystes
concepts.definition: An initiate in the Eleusinian Mysteries.

concepts.name: Mystagogos
concepts.definition: Patron who guided an initiate in the Eleusinian Mysteries.

concepts.name: Haloa
concepts.definition: A women's festival in honor of Demeter, also celebrating Dionysus, characterized by abundant food and drink and ribald behavior.

concepts.name: Nekyia
concepts.definition: A ritual invocation of the dead, as performed by Odysseus in Book 11 of the Odyssey.

concepts.name: asphodel
concepts.definition: A plant that grows in the Underworld plain where souls dwell.

concepts.name: Homeric Underworld
concepts.definition: The afterlife as depicted in Homer's Odyssey, a vague and gloomy realm where all mortals end up together without clear judgment or reward/punishment.

concepts.name: cult of the dead
concepts.definition: Religious practices involving sacrifices and ceremonies for the dead, seen in the Odyssey's Book of the Dead.

concepts.name: judgment of the dead
concepts.definition: The concept of souls being judged after death, as seen in the Myth of Er where judges send the just upward and the unjust downward.

concepts.name: reincarnation
concepts.definition: The belief that souls are reborn after a cycle of punishment and reward, implied in the Myth of Er's thousand-year cycle.

concepts.name: Last Judgment
concepts.definition: Christian concept of final judgment, influenced by classical myths of the Underworld.

concepts.name: spindle of Necessity
concepts.definition: A cosmic device by which all revolving spheres are turned, held on the knees of Necessity.

concepts.name: harmony of the spheres
concepts.definition: The unified musical harmony produced by eight Sirens perched on the circles of the spindle.

concepts.name: daimon
concepts.definition: A divinity or guiding spirit chosen by each soul for its life.

concepts.name: transmigration of the soul
concepts.definition: The belief that the soul passes into a new body after death; associated with Pythagoras.

concepts.name: Orphic
concepts.definition: Relating to Orpheus or the mystery religion associated with him; involves reward, punishment, and purification.

concepts.name: golden bough
concepts.definition: A sacred branch that Aeneas must obtain to enter the Underworld; sacred to Proserpine.

concepts.name: Furies
concepts.definition: Goddesses of vengeance, including Tisiphone, who punish sinners in Tartarus.

concepts.name: Elysian Fields
concepts.definition: Paradise in the Underworld for the virtuous and blessed.

concepts.name: Transmigration of souls
concepts.definition: The belief that souls are reborn into new bodies after death, as described by Anchises in the Aeneid.

concepts.name: Pythagorean
concepts.definition: Philosophical and religious beliefs attributed to Pythagoras, including transmigration of souls.

concepts.name: Eumenides
concepts.definition: Euphemistic name for the Furies, meaning 'kindly ones', used in Athens after they were appeased.

concepts.name: Areopagus
concepts.definition: The court of Athens that decided Orestes' case, representing the new regime of law.

concepts.name: shamanism
concepts.definition: A religious belief system of great antiquity, practiced in northern Asian and native North American cultures; parallels with Orpheus and his religion.

concepts.name: shaman
concepts.definition: Mystical figure with supernatural powers, entering trance-like states to journey into spirit realm for divination and healing.

concepts.name: syncretism
concepts.definition: Harmonizing of different cults and their myths into some sort of unity; literally 'growing together'.

concepts.name: taurobolium
concepts.definition: Rite of initiation into mysteries of Cybele and Attis, involving shedding of bull's blood over initiate in a pit.

concepts.name: tauroctony
concepts.definition: Scene depicting Mithras killing a bull, basic to iconography of a Mithraeum.

concepts.name: heroine
concepts.definition: Female counterpart to hero, often of royal or divine stature, with motifs of seclusion, pregnancy by a god, punishment, and rescue.

concepts.name: Spartoi
concepts.definition: The 'sown men' who sprang from the serpent's teeth sown by Cadmus; five survived and became ancestors of Theban nobility.

concepts.name: Iconography of the Rape of Europa
concepts.definition: Artistic tradition depicting Europa's abduction, typically showing her either garlanding the bull or riding it through the sea.

concepts.name: Curse of Pelops
concepts.definition: Curse invoked by Pelops against Laius for abducting his son Chrysippus, leading to the doom of Laius and his descendants.

concepts.name: Riddle of the Sphinx
concepts.definition: Riddle taught by the Muses: 'What is it that has one name that is four-footed, two-footed, and three-footed?' Answer: Man.

concepts.name: Guest-host relationship
concepts.definition: Sacred bond between guest and host; Laius violated it by abducting Chrysippus.

concepts.name: unwritten laws
concepts.definition: Divine laws that compel Antigone to bury her brother despite human law.

concepts.name: hero cult
concepts.definition: Oedipus becomes a hero after death, associated with a locality and performing miracles.

concepts.name: Nemean Games
concepts.definition: Athletic contests founded by the Seven in honor of Opheltes.

concepts.name: Curse of Oedipus
concepts.definition: The curse placed by Oedipus on his sons Eteocles and Polynices, which led to their mutual killing.

concepts.name: Unwritten laws of the gods
concepts.definition: Divine laws that supersede human decrees, as invoked by Antigone.

concepts.name: Epigoni
concepts.definition: The sons of the Seven against Thebes who led a successful expedition against Thebes ten years later.

concepts.name: curse of the House of Atreus
concepts.definition: A hereditary curse originating from the murder of Myrtilus and the crimes of Tantalus, leading to a cycle of vengeance and tragedy.

concepts.name: cannibalism in myth
concepts.definition: Recurring motif in Greek myths, including the stories of Tantalus, Lycaon, and the banquet of Thyestes, possibly reflecting ancient sacrificial rituals.

concepts.name: Pelopion
concepts.definition: Shrine of Pelops at Olympia, located next to the temple of Zeus.

concepts.name: blood-guilt
concepts.definition: Guilt inherited from murder, central to the curse on the House of Atreus.

concepts.name: Heraclidae
concepts.definition: Descendants of Heracles who fought against Tisamenus.

concepts.name: justice
concepts.definition: Central theme in the Oresteia, involving divine and human retribution.

concepts.name: dramatic irony
concepts.definition: A literary device where the audience knows more than the characters; used in Sophocles' Electra.

concepts.name: matricide
concepts.definition: The act of killing one's mother.

concepts.name: Dioscuri
concepts.definition: Sons of Zeus, Castor and Polydeuces; patron deities of sailors and seafarers, appearing as St. Elmo's fire.

concepts.name: Tyndaridae
concepts.definition: Patronymic for Castor and Polydeuces, meaning sons of Tyndareus (their mortal stepfather).

concepts.name: St. Elmo's fire
concepts.definition: Electrical discharge seen on ships; associated with the Dioscuri as a sign of deliverance.

concepts.name: Palinode
concepts.definition: A poem retracting a previous statement; Stesichorus' Palinode claimed Helen never went to Troy.

concepts.name: teichoskopia
concepts.definition: Viewing from the wall; scene in Iliad Book 3 where Helen identifies Greek leaders for Priam.

concepts.name: heroic ethos
concepts.definition: The set of values and ideals associated with Greek heroes, including honor, glory, and excellence in battle and speech.

concepts.name: invulnerability
concepts.definition: The state of being unable to be wounded; Achilles was made invulnerable except for his heel by being dipped in the Styx.

concepts.name: wrath
concepts.definition: The central theme of the Iliad, referring to Achilles' anger at Agamemnon, which causes countless deaths.

concepts.name: Glory (kleos)
concepts.definition: Immortal fame earned through heroic deeds, especially in battle.

concepts.name: Compassion
concepts.definition: Achilles learns compassion through suffering, as seen in the ransom scene.

concepts.name: Greek tragic view of life
concepts.definition: Pessimistic view that human existence is filled with suffering and that happiness is fleeting.

concepts.name: theomachy
concepts.definition: A battle among the gods, as depicted in the Iliad, highlighting the contrast between mortal suffering and divine triviality.

concepts.name: sophrones
concepts.definition: Greek term for moderate or self-controlled individuals, loved by the gods.

concepts.name: meleagrides
concepts.definition: Guinea fowl, into which the women mourning Meleager were transformed.

concepts.name: Nostoi
concepts.definition: Epic called Returns, narrating the returns of Greek leaders from Troy; only a brief prose summary and three lines of verse extant.

concepts.name: Nekuia
concepts.definition: A rite by which ghosts were summoned and questioned; also the name for Odysseus' visit to the Underworld in Book 11 of the Odyssey.

concepts.name: moly
concepts.definition: A magic herb given by Hermes to Odysseus to counter Circe's charms; its root is black and flower white as milk.

concepts.name: guest-friendship
concepts.definition: Sacred bond of hospitality between host and guest, exemplified by Telemachus greeting Athena.

concepts.name: polytropos
concepts.definition: Epithet of Odysseus meaning 'man of many twists and turns' or 'much-turning'.

concepts.name: periphron
concepts.definition: Epithet of Penelope meaning 'circumspect' or 'wary'.

concepts.name: thymares
concepts.definition: Term describing Penelope as 'fitting his heart', a perfect match for Odysseus.

concepts.name: Outis
concepts.definition: Greek for 'Nobody', the false name Odysseus gives to the Cyclops.

concepts.name: Cap of Invisibility
concepts.definition: Magic object given to Perseus by nymphs, made him invisible.

concepts.name: winged sandals
concepts.definition: Magic sandals given to Perseus by nymphs, allowed him to fly.

concepts.name: kibisis
concepts.definition: Wallet or bag given to Perseus by nymphs, used to carry Medusa's head.

concepts.name: scimitar
concepts.definition: Weapon given to Perseus by Hermes.

concepts.name: brazen shield
concepts.definition: Shield used by Perseus to reflect Medusa's gaze.

concepts.name: folktale motifs
concepts.definition: Recurring story elements in folklore, such as magic conception, villainous king, rash promise, supernatural helpers, etc., found in the Perseus saga.

concepts.name: athloi
concepts.definition: Greek word for labors, meaning contests undertaken for a prize; in Heracles' case, the prize was immortality.

concepts.name: parergon
concepts.definition: Side adventure; used to describe the centaur episode during the Erymanthian Boar labor.

concepts.name: parerga
concepts.definition: Additional adventures or side deeds of Heracles during his labors.

concepts.name: Labors of Heracles
concepts.definition: Twelve tasks imposed on Heracles by Eurystheus, including the Apples of the Hesperides and Cerberus.

concepts.name: Conquest of death
concepts.definition: Theme in Heracles' labors, especially the Apples of the Hesperides and Cerberus, symbolizing overcoming mortality.

concepts.name: Apotheosis
concepts.definition: The transformation of a mortal into a god, as Heracles achieved after his death.

concepts.name: Master of Animals
concepts.definition: A concept suggesting Heracles' association with animals and his role in taming them for human use.

concepts.name: Stoicism
concepts.definition: Philosophical school that valued Heraclean qualities of endurance and virtue.

concepts.name: Kairos
concepts.definition: The Right Time, personified as a deity favoring Iolaüs in Pindar's version.

concepts.name: Pillars of Heracles
concepts.definition: Boundary markers set by Heracles at the Strait of Gibraltar, associated with the tenth labor.

concepts.name: Gallic Heracles
concepts.definition: A depiction of Heracles as an old man with chains from his tongue, symbolizing rhetoric, used in French political imagery.

concepts.name: Cornucopia
concepts.definition: Horn of plenty, derived from the horn of Acheloüs.

concepts.name: autochthonous
concepts.definition: Sprung from the earth; Athenians claimed to be autochthonous, not descended from invaders.

concepts.name: Delphic oracle
concepts.definition: Oracle of Apollo at Delphi; consulted by Aegeus and by Xuthus and Creusa.

concepts.name: synoecism
concepts.definition: The union of different villages into one political unit with Athens as its center, credited to Theseus.

concepts.name: Isthmian Games
concepts.definition: Athletic games held at the Isthmus of Corinth, refounded by Theseus.

concepts.name: Crane dance
concepts.definition: A dance performed by Theseus and his companions on Delos, imitating the windings of the Labyrinth.

concepts.name: talisman
concepts.definition: An object believed to have magical protective properties; here, Nisus' purple lock of hair was the talisman of Megara.

concepts.name: Minyae
concepts.definition: Name for the Argonauts, referring to their descent from Minyan ancestors; cities like Iolcus and Miletus claimed Minyan descent.

concepts.name: Folktale elements
concepts.definition: Elements in the Argonautic saga that fit a coherent structure when viewed as a quest.

concepts.name: sophist
concepts.definition: A teacher of rhetoric known for making the worse argument seem the better; Jason is described as an exemplary sophist.

concepts.name: suppliant
concepts.definition: A person who seeks refuge or protection by appealing to a higher power or authority; Medea becomes a suppliant to Aegeus.

concepts.name: Oath by Earth, Helius, and the gods
concepts.definition: A solemn oath sworn by Jason, invoking Earth, the sacred light of Helius, and all the gods.

concepts.name: Justice of Zeus
concepts.definition: Concept invoked by Medea, referring to divine justice.

concepts.name: Cypress Tree
concepts.definition: The tree into which Cyparissus was transformed after grieving his stag.

concepts.name: Laurel
concepts.definition: The laurel tree into which Daphne was transformed; sacred to Apollo.

concepts.name: Pomegranate
concepts.definition: The fruit whose seeds bound Persephone to the Underworld.

concepts.name: the Birth and Childhood of Hermes

artworks.name: Snake Goddess from the Palace at Cnossos
artworks.description: Glazed earthenware figure (faience), ca. 1600 B.C., discovered by Sir Arthur Evans in 1903, now in the Archaeological Museum of Heraklion. Depicts a female with elaborate headdress, flounced skirt, open bodice, exposed breasts, holding snakes.

artworks.name: North Entrance Passage fresco at Cnossus
artworks.description: Fresco of a bull's head, part of a scene of a charging bull or bull-grappling, reconstructed on site.

artworks.name: Lion Gate relief at Mycenae
artworks.description: Relief of two lions or lionesses flanking a column at the entrance to Mycenae; possibly the emblem of the royal family.

artworks.name: Gold masks from Mycenae shaft graves
artworks.description: Masks of beaten gold placed on faces of corpses in shaft graves at Mycenae.

artworks.name: Reconstruction of the Megaron at Pylos
artworks.description: Watercolor reconstruction by Piet de Jong of the megaron at Pylos, showing central hearth and throne position.

artworks.name: Model of Troy VI
artworks.description: A model illustrating the results of Manfred Korfmann's excavations, showing the citadel and lower town of Troy VI.

artworks.name: Luwian seal from Troy
artworks.description: A small round bronze seal, biconvex, with Luwian inscription, dated to the second half of the twelfth century B.C.

artworks.name: Fresco of a lyre player at Pylos
artworks.description: A fresco found at Pylos depicting a lyre player, illustrating the role of music in Mycenaean civilization.

artworks.name: Helius red-figure krater
artworks.description: Red-figure krater by the Darius painter, ca. 330 B.C., depicting Helius driving his chariot upward out of the sea, with diving boys.

artworks.name: Endymion Sarcophagus
artworks.description: Marble sarcophagus from ca. A.D. 200-220, depicting Selene descending to Endymion, with various mythological reliefs.

artworks.name: Aurora by Guido Reni
artworks.description: Painting from 1614 showing Aurora (Eos) preceding Apollo (Helius) with his chariot and the Hours.

artworks.name: Saturn Devouring His Children
artworks.description: Oil on plaster transferred to canvas by Francisco Goya (1820-1822); depicts Cronus cannibalizing his child; part of Las Pinturas Negras.

artworks.name: Rhea Offers the Stone to Cronus
artworks.description: Roman copy (c. A.D. 160) of Greek original (4th century B.C.); shows Rhea handing swaddled stone to Cronus.

artworks.name: Saturn Devouring His Son
artworks.description: Painting by Rubens that may have inspired Goya's work.

artworks.name: Palaikastro Kouros
artworks.description: Chryselephantine statuette of a young god from Minoan Age, found near sanctuary of Zeus Dictaeus.

artworks.name: The Ancient of Days
artworks.description: Relief etching by William Blake, frontispiece to Europe: A Prophecy, depicting Urizen as creator with compasses.

artworks.name: Bronze statue of Zeus from Cape Artemisium
artworks.description: Bronze statue of Zeus hurling a thunderbolt, ca. 460 B.C., height 82 in., found off Cape Artemisium.

artworks.name: Great Altar of Pergamum
artworks.description: Monumental altar with a 100-meter marble frieze of the Gigantomachy, erected by Eumenes II.

artworks.name: Telephus frieze
artworks.description: Smaller frieze (58 meters) on the Great Altar of Pergamum depicting the myth of Telephus.

artworks.name: Great Altar of Zeus at Pergamon
artworks.description: Monumental altar commissioned by Eumenes II, ca. 175 B.C., with a frieze depicting the Gigantomachy, about 400 feet long and 7 feet high.

artworks.name: Athena Defeats Alcyoneus
artworks.description: Detail from the east frieze of the Great Altar of Pergamon, between 180 and 159 B.C.; height 8 ft. 2 in. Shows Athena striding right, seizing Alcyoneus's hair, with Nike flying to crown her.

artworks.name: Atlas and Prometheus cup
artworks.description: Laconian black-figure cup, ca. 560 B.C., depicting Atlas holding up the heavens and watching a vulture attack Prometheus bound to a column.

artworks.name: Pandora by Odilon Redon
artworks.description: Oil on canvas, ca. 1910, depicting Pandora holding her box, framed by jewellike flowers with a leafless tree above.

artworks.name: Mercury and Argus
artworks.description: Oil on canvas by Diego Velázquez; depicts Mercury stealthily approaching Argus as he falls asleep, with Io as a cow in the background.

artworks.name: Zeus and Hera metope from Temple E at Selinus
artworks.description: Limestone and marble metope from Temple E at Selinus, ca. 470 B.C., portraying the hieros gamos of Zeus and Hera. Zeus sits on Mt. Ida drawing Hera toward him; Hera stands facing Zeus with her veil drawn back, wearing archaic clothing.

artworks.name: Statue of Zeus at Olympia
artworks.description: Monumental chryselephantine statue by Pheidias, about 42 feet high, seated Zeus holding Nike and scepter with eagle, throne decorated with various myths.

artworks.name: West pediment of temple of Zeus at Olympia
artworks.description: Depicts the battle of Greeks and centaurs at the wedding of Pirithoüs, with Apollo central.

artworks.name: East pediment of temple of Zeus at Olympia
artworks.description: Shows the scene before the chariot race of Pelops and Hippodamia, with Zeus central.

artworks.name: Metopes of temple of Zeus at Olympia
artworks.description: Doric frieze with the Twelve Labors of Heracles, each about 1.6 meters high.

artworks.name: Jupiter and Thetis
artworks.description: Oil on canvas by Ingres (1811), depicting Jupiter enthroned with scepter and eagle, Thetis supplicating, with Juno partially visible.

artworks.name: Barberini Hera
artworks.description: Roman copy of a Greek original, Hera carrying scepter and patera, wearing crown and chiton.

artworks.name: Zeus and Ganymede (kylix)
artworks.description: Red-figure kylix by the Penthesilea painter, ca. 460-440 B.C., depicting the abduction of Ganymede by Zeus. Zeus holds a stylized thunderbolt and scepter; Ganymede holds a cockerel.

artworks.name: Hephaestus' Return to Olympus (krater)
artworks.description: Attic black-figure krater by Lydos, ca. 550 B.C., showing a drunk Hephaestus on a mule, accompanied by a thiasos of satyrs and maenads.

artworks.name: The Finding of Vulcan on the Island of Lemnos
artworks.description: Painting by Piero di Cosimo (1462-1522), depicting Hephaestus as a boy thrown from Olympus and rescued by Sintian women.

artworks.name: The Forge of Vulcan
artworks.description: Oil on canvas by Diego Velázquez (1599–1660), depicting Helius telling Hephaestus of Aphrodite's affair with Ares.

artworks.name: Ludovisi Mars
artworks.description: Roman copy of a Greek original (possibly by Skopas) of ca. 340 B.C., marble, showing Mars (Ares) unarmed but holding his sword, with Cupid added by the copyist.

artworks.name: Temple of Zeus at Olympia
artworks.description: Temple completed in 456 BC, housing the statue of Zeus. Its sculptures are discussed in art history.

artworks.name: Croesus on the Pyre
artworks.description: Attic red-figure amphora by Myson, ca. 500 B.C., depicting Croesus enthroned on a pyre, pouring a libation.

artworks.name: Parthenon
artworks.description: Temple of Athena on the Acropolis, with pediments showing Athena's birth and contest with Poseidon, and frieze depicting the Panathenaea.

artworks.name: Statue of a man on a dolphin
artworks.description: Statue said to have been dedicated by Arion in the temple of Poseidon at Taenarum.

artworks.name: Preparation for Sacrifice
artworks.description: Red-figure krater attributed to the Kleophon painter or his school, ca. 425 B.C.; depicts a ram led to sacrifice, with altar, officiating priest, water basin, kanoun, bukranion, auletes, and youth.

artworks.name: A Sacrifice to Apollo
artworks.description: Red-figure Attic krater, ca. 430 B.C.; depicts a sacrifice scene with Apollo holding a laurel branch, altar, laurel tree, officiating priest, youths roasting splanchna, and kanoun.

artworks.name: Neptune in His Chariot
artworks.description: Central panel of a large square mosaic of Neptune and the Seasons, mid-second century A.D., diameter 77 in. Neptune dominates with four sea-horses pulling his chariot, with a sea-nymph and a Triton.

artworks.name: Galatea
artworks.description: Fresco by Raphaël, ca. 1512, in the Sala di Galatea, Villa Farnesina, Rome. Depicts Galatea riding a seashell chariot drawn by dolphins, surrounded by Tritons, lovers, and cupids.

artworks.name: Polyphemus
artworks.description: Fresco by Sebastiano del Piombo, painted to the left of Raphaël's Galatea, depicting the Cyclops Polyphemus.

artworks.name: The Triumph of Neptune and Amphitrite
artworks.description: Oil on canvas by Nicolas Poussin, ca. 1637. Depicts Amphitrite at center in a shell chariot drawn by dolphins, with Neptune in a chariot drawn by sea-horses, surrounded by Nereids, Tritons, and cupids.

artworks.name: Neptune and Triton
artworks.description: Marble sculpture by Gian Lorenzo Bernini, 1619. Depicts Neptune striding forward angrily, supported by Triton blowing his conch.

artworks.name: Athena Parthenos
artworks.description: Monumental gold and ivory statue of Athena by Pheidias in the Parthenon, holding Nike, with aegis, shield, spear, and serpent.

artworks.name: Parthenon east pediment
artworks.description: Depicts the birth of Athena from Zeus's head, with Helius's horses rising and Selene's sinking.

artworks.name: Parthenon west pediment
artworks.description: Depicts the contest of Athena and Poseidon for Athens.

artworks.name: Parthenon metopes
artworks.description: Ninety-two metopes with reliefs: south (Centauromachy), north (Sack of Troy), east (Gigantomachy), west (Amazonomachy).

artworks.name: Parthenon Ionic frieze
artworks.description: Continuous frieze around the cella depicting the Panathenaic procession.

artworks.name: Black-figure amphora (Birth of Athena)
artworks.description: Athenian black-figure amphora showing Athena emerging from Zeus's head, with Hermes, Apollo, Eileithyia, and Ares.

artworks.name: Las Hilanderas (The Weavers)
artworks.description: Painting by Velázquez depicting weavers and the myth of Athena and Arachne in the background.

artworks.name: Pallas Athena
artworks.description: Oil on canvas by Gustav Klimt, 29.5 x 29.5 in., depicting Athena with archaic elements, gold highlights, and a nude Nike.

artworks.name: Mourning Athena
artworks.description: Marble relief from the Acropolis, ca. 460 B.C., height 21 in., showing Athena without aegis or shield, gazing at a stele.

artworks.name: Athena and Heracles kylix
artworks.description: Interior of a kylix by potter Python and painter Duris, ca. 475 B.C., diameter 13 in., showing Athena pouring wine for Heracles.

artworks.name: Temple of Athena Nike
artworks.description: Simple temple on a bastion at the entrance to the Acropolis.

artworks.name: Ludovisi Throne
artworks.description: Three-sided marble relief (ca. 460 B.C.) showing Aphrodite rising from the sea, attended by two women; also includes a musician and a veiled woman on side panels.

artworks.name: Aphrodite of Melos (Venus de Milo)
artworks.description: Late second century B.C. marble statue of Aphrodite, half draped; best known Hellenistic representation.

artworks.name: Aphrodite of Cnidus
artworks.description: Statue by Praxiteles (mid-fourth century B.C.) that popularized nude female form; survives only in copies.

artworks.name: Venus and Adonis by Paolo Veronese
artworks.description: Oil on canvas, 1584. Adonis sleeps in Venus's lap; a cupid restrains a hound.

artworks.name: The Heart Desires by Edward Burne-Jones
artworks.description: Oil on canvas, 39x30 in. Pygmalion contemplates creation before a plinth.

artworks.name: The Hand Refrains by Edward Burne-Jones
artworks.description: Oil on canvas, 39x30 in. Pygmalion hesitates to touch his statue.

artworks.name: The Godhead Fires by Edward Burne-Jones
artworks.description: Oil on canvas, 39x30 in. Venus brings Galatea to life with a touch.

artworks.name: The Soul Attains by Edward Burne-Jones
artworks.description: Oil on canvas, 39x30 in. Pygmalion reaches to touch Galatea.

artworks.name: Venus and Anchises
artworks.description: Fresco by Annibale Carracci in the Farnese Palace, Rome, depicting the seduction of Anchises by Venus (Aphrodite).

artworks.name: Amor Vincit Omnia (Love Conquers All)
artworks.description: Oil on canvas by Caravaggio (ca. 1601–1602); depicts a prepubescent Cupid with eagle's wings treading on symbols of human achievement.

artworks.name: Cupid and Psyche by Jacques-Louis David
artworks.description: Oil on canvas, 1817; depicts Cupid and Psyche after lovemaking, with Psyche sleeping and a butterfly hovering above; Cupid's expression is that of a satiated conqueror.

artworks.name: Aphrodite of Knidos
artworks.description: Statue of Aphrodite by Praxiteles, modeled on Phryne.

artworks.name: Artemis the Huntress
artworks.description: Roman copy in marble of a Greek bronze of the late fourth century B.C.; height 78 in. Artemis appears as huntress taking an arrow from her quiver and as protectress of animals grasping a leaping stag.

artworks.name: Death of the Children of Niobe
artworks.description: Attic red-figure krater by the Niobid painter, ca. 460 B.C.; height 21¼ in. Depicts Artemis and Apollo killing the Niobids in a rocky landscape.

artworks.name: Death of Actaeon krater
artworks.description: Athenian red-figure krater by the Pan painter, ca. 460 B.C.; shows Artemis shooting Actaeon as his hounds tear him.

artworks.name: François vase handle
artworks.description: Handle of the François vase by Ergotimos and Kleitias, ca. 575 B.C.; depicts Artemis as Potnia Theron holding a panther and a stag.

artworks.name: Artemis of Ephesus statue
artworks.description: Statue of Artemis at Ephesus with a robe of animal heads and multiple breasts.

artworks.name: Artemis of Ephesus
artworks.description: Alabaster and bronze statue from mid-second century A.D., depicting Artemis with multiple breastlike objects, rows of animal heads, turreted polos, and figure of Nike.

artworks.name: Apulian volute-krater by the Darius painter
artworks.description: Lower register shows the death of Hippolytus: an old retainer runs behind the chariot, Hippolytus loses control as horses panic at a bull from the sea, a Fury holds a flaming torch. Upper register shows six gods including Aphrodite, Artemis, Poseidon.

artworks.name: Aegeus before Themis
artworks.description: Red-figure kylix by the Codrus painter, ca. 440 B.C., 12.8 in. diameter. Depicts Aegeus consulting Themis at Delphi; she holds a phiale and laurel branch, seated on a tripod.

artworks.name: Apollo and Daphne by Bernini
artworks.description: Marble sculpture by Gian-Lorenzo Bernini (1624); height 96 in. Depicts the moment of Daphne's metamorphosis into a laurel tree, with Apollo in pursuit. Inscribed with Ovid's description and two Latin lines by Pope Urban VIII.

artworks.name: Votive relief from Oropus
artworks.description: Votive relief dedicated by Archinus to Amphiaraüs, depicting the healing process: Archinus asleep, a snake biting his shoulder, and Amphiaraüs tending to him.

artworks.name: The Flaying of Marsyas
artworks.description: Painting by Titian (ca. 1480–1576), 85 × 83 in. Depicts Apollo flaying Marsyas, with a dog licking blood, followers playing instruments, Midas contemplating, and an old satyr with a bucket.

artworks.name: Christus Apollo
artworks.description: Vault mosaic from a third-century A.D. Christian tomb beneath St. Peter's Basilica, showing Christ with attributes of the sun-god (Apollo or Helius), ascending in a chariot drawn by four white horses, with ivy of Dionysus in the background.

artworks.name: Apollo Belvedere
artworks.description: Roman marble copy, possibly second century A.D., of a fourth-century B.C. Greek bronze. Height 94½ in. Apollo strides ahead, left hand would have held a bow. Discovered in Rome before 1509, housed in the Vatican's Cortile del Belvedere.

artworks.name: Apollo from the west pediment of the temple of Zeus at Olympia
artworks.description: Central figure from the west pediment of the temple of Zeus at Olympia, ca. 460 B.C. Height ca. 120 in. Apollo stands calmly amidst the battle of Centaurs and Lapiths, imposing peace.

artworks.name: Apollo Delphinius
artworks.description: Attic red-figure hydria by the Berlin painter, ca. 480 B.C.; height 20 ½ in. Apollo rides over the sea in a winged tripod, as dolphins leap above the waves and fishes and an octopus swims below. He wears the laurel wreath and plays the lyre, while his bow and quiver are slung on his back.

artworks.name: Tomb of Dionysus
artworks.description: Religious object that decked the temple of Apollo at Delphi; tomb of Dionysus.

artworks.name: Hermes and the Infant Dionysus
artworks.description: Statue by Praxiteles, ca. 340 B.C., height 82 in., seen by Pausanias in the temple of Hera at Olympia. Depicts Hermes holding the infant Dionysus, who reaches for grapes. Made of white Parian marble.

artworks.name: Hermes in Crib with Zeus, Apollo, and Maia
artworks.description: Black-figure hydria from Caere, ca. 500 B.C., 17 in. in height. Depicts Apollo accusing baby Hermes before Zeus and Maia, with stolen cattle behind a tree.

artworks.name: Hermes (Attic red-figure cup by the Euaion painter)
artworks.description: Attic red-figure cup from ca. 460 B.C. depicting Hermes with his attributes of petasus, caduceus, and winged boots, wearing a traveler's cloak and bearded.

artworks.name: Mercury by Giovanni Bologna
artworks.description: Bronze sculpture from 1576, height 25 inches. Giambologna combines classical attributes of Hermes (petasus, caduceus, winged sandals) with a nude running figure, a masterpiece of Late Renaissance Mannerism.

artworks.name: Herms. Athenian red-figure krater
artworks.description: Red-figure krater showing a young woman clasping the shoulders of Hermes beside a herm.

artworks.name: Herms. Red-figure amphora by the Pan painter
artworks.description: Red-figure amphora showing a young man between two herms, touching the god's beard in supplication.

artworks.name: A Hermaphrodite. Roman marble copy of a Greek bronze by Polycles
artworks.description: Roman marble copy of a Greek bronze by Polycles, with marble mattress added by Bernini. Depicts Hermaphroditus with both male and female attributes.

artworks.name: Statues of Hermaphroditus
artworks.description: Statues of Hermaphroditus and hermaphrodites became common in the fourth century and Hellenistic period, executed in realistic, erotic, and unusual styles.

artworks.name: The Death of Semele
artworks.description: Oil on panel by Peter Paul Rubens (1636), depicting Semele and Zeus under extreme emotion as she dies from Zeus's lightning.

artworks.name: The Indian Triumph of Dionysus
artworks.description: Roman marble sarcophagus (mid-second century A.D.) showing Dionysus on a chariot drawn by panthers, preceded by satyrs, maenads, sileni, and animals. Lid shows scenes of Semele's death, birth of Dionysus, and his nurture by nymphs.

artworks.name: The Birth of Dionysus
artworks.description: Attic red-figure lekythos by the Alkimachos painter (ca. 460 B.C.), showing Zeus giving birth to Dionysus from his thigh, with Hermes present.

artworks.name: The Second Birth of Dionysus
artworks.description: Photograph by George Platt Lynes (1907-1955), depicting the birth of Dionysus from Zeus's thigh with erotic and surrealist aesthetic.

artworks.name: Dionysus and Maenads
artworks.description: Attic red-figure amphora by the Kleophrades painter (ca. 490 B.C.), showing Dionysus with a kantharos and vine branch, flanked by maenads and satyrs.

artworks.name: Dionysus, Maenads, and Satyrs
artworks.description: Attic black-figure kylix by Nikosthenes, ca. 520 B.C. Depicts Dionysus sitting on a square chair holding a rhyton, with dancing ithyphallic satyrs and maenads, vine-leaves and grapes, and a running winged Gorgon in the center.

artworks.name: Pentheus kylix by Douris
artworks.description: Attic red-figure kylix (drinking cup) depicting the dismemberment of Pentheus by maenads, with a satyr observing. On the opposite side, Dionysus enjoys wine to music. On the tondo, a maenad holds a leopard and a thyrsus.

artworks.name: Dionysus and Satyrs (red-figure kylix by the Brygos painter)
artworks.description: Red-figure kylix from ca. 480 B.C. depicting a Bacchic revel with Dionysus playing a lyre, flanked by two satyrs with castanets. Dionysus is wreathed with ivy; satyrs are balding, snub-nosed, with goat's beard, horse tail and ears.

artworks.name: Maenad (Attic kylix by Brygos painter)
artworks.description: White-ground painting showing a maenad in motion, holding a thyrsus and a small leopard, with a leopardskin and serpent wreath.

artworks.name: Dionysus and Maenads (black-figure amphora by Amasis painter)
artworks.description: Dionysus holding a kantharos, saluting two maenads who dance and hold ivy and a small deer.

artworks.name: Dionysus (kylix by Exekias)
artworks.description: Depicts Dionysus reclining on a ship with a grape-laden vine around the mast; crew transformed into dolphins.

artworks.name: Pan Pursuing a Goatherd
artworks.description: Attic red-figure krater by the Pan painter, ca. 460 B.C., depicting Pan pursuing a herdsman, possibly Daphnis, with a herm or Priapus in the background.

artworks.name: Echo and Narcissus by Nicolas Poussin
artworks.description: Oil on canvas, ca. 1630, showing Narcissus lying by a pool with flowers, Echo fading in the background, and Cupid with a burning torch.

artworks.name: Demeter statue from Cnidus
artworks.description: Marble cult statue from the sanctuary of Demeter at Cnidus, second half of the fourth century B.C., height 58 in. Depicts Demeter seated and heavily draped with solemn gaze.

artworks.name: Hades and Persephone by Gian-Lorenzo Bernini
artworks.description: Marble statue (1621-1622) depicting Hades seizing Persephone, with Cerberus at lower right. Height 87 in.

artworks.name: Pluto and Proserpina by Jeff Koons
artworks.description: Stainless steel sculpture brushed with yellow-gold paint, decorated with live flowering plants. Height 129 in. Based on an 18th-century porcelain figurine.

artworks.name: Hades and Persephone terracotta plaque
artworks.description: Terracotta plaque from Locri, ca. 460 B.C., showing Hades and Persephone enthroned with emblems: grain, parsley, a cock, a bowl.

artworks.name: Persephone, Hermes, and Hecate krater
artworks.description: Athenian red-figure krater, ca. 440 B.C., depicting Persephone emerging from the Underworld with Hermes and Hecate.

artworks.name: The Departure of Triptolemus cup
artworks.description: Attic red-figure cup by Makron, ca. 480 B.C., showing Triptolemus with grain, Persephone pouring a libation, Demeter holding torch and grain, and personification of Eleusis.

artworks.name: Niinnion Pinax
artworks.description: Red-figure clay votive tablet from ca. 370 B.C., dedicated by Niinnion to Demeter and Persephone, depicting scenes possibly from the Eleusinian Mysteries.

artworks.name: Underworld krater by the Underworld painter
artworks.description: Apulian red-figure krater, ca. 320 B.C., depicting Hades and Persephone enthroned, Orpheus, Heracles with Cerberus, Sisyphus, Tantalus, and other Underworld scenes.

artworks.name: Underworld vase
artworks.description: Painted vase depicting the Underworld, focusing on Orpheus, Heracles, and sinners against the gods.

artworks.name: Last Judgment by Luca Signorelli
artworks.description: Fresco cycle in Orvieto cathedral depicting the end of the world, including the assembly of the damned.

artworks.name: Last Judgment by Michelangelo
artworks.description: Fresco in the Sistine Chapel depicting the Last Judgment.

artworks.name: Aeneas and the Sibyl in the Underworld
artworks.description: Oil on canvas by Jan Brueghel the Elder (1600); depicts Aeneas with sword and golden bough, with Tartarus fires and monsters.

artworks.name: Cerberus
artworks.description: Watercolor by William Blake (1825-1827); illustration for Dante's Inferno; shows Cerberus with three heads.

artworks.name: Ixion vase
artworks.description: Attic red-figure vase by the Amphitrite painter, ca. 460 B.C., depicting Ixion naked, looking toward Hera seated on her throne, with Athena holding the winged wheel, Hermes holding Ixion's left wrist, and Ares holding his right wrist.

artworks.name: Spring: Orpheus and Eurydice
artworks.description: Oil on canvas by Eugène Delacroix (1863), depicting Eurydice falling as a companion looks at a snake, with Orpheus approaching with his lyre.

artworks.name: Orpheus Charms the Wild Animals
artworks.description: Mosaic from Antioch (second century A.D.), showing Orpheus dressed as a Thracian, sitting on a rock and playing the lyre, pacifying beasts and birds.

artworks.name: Orpheus, Eurydice, and Hermes
artworks.description: Marble relief, Roman copy of a Greek original of the fifth century B.C.; height 46 ½ in.; originally part of a parapet around the Altar of the Twelve Gods in the Agora at Athens; shows Orpheus looking back at Eurydice with Hermes Psychopompos.

artworks.name: Orpheus among the Thracians
artworks.description: Athenian red-figure krater by the Orpheus painter, ca. 440 B.C.; shows Orpheus seated on a rock, garlanded with ivy, singing with a seven-stringed lyre to four Thracians.

artworks.name: Mithras Killing the Bull
artworks.description: Marble relief, second century A.D., showing Mithras plunging dagger into bull's throat; bull's tail changes into ears of wheat; below are scorpion, snake, dog; medallions of sun and moon.

artworks.name: Wall mosaic in cemetery beneath St. Peter's basilica
artworks.description: Third century A.D. wall mosaic showing vine of Dionysus associated with Christian resurrection.

artworks.name: Sarcophagus with Dionysus finding Ariadne
artworks.description: Second-century sarcophagus decorated with relief showing Dionysus finding Ariadne; found in cemetery beneath St. Peter's.

artworks.name: The Rape of Europa (Selinus metope)
artworks.description: Limestone metope from Selinus, ca. 540 B.C., showing Europa riding the bull over dolphins.

artworks.name: The Rape of Europa (Titian)
artworks.description: Oil on canvas, 1559-1562, by Titian, depicting Europa's abduction with cupids and distant companions.

artworks.name: Abduction of Chrysippus (Apulian bell-krater)
artworks.description: Apulian bell-krater by the Darius painter, ca. 340 B.C., showing Laius abducting Chrysippus in a chariot with gods and others.

artworks.name: Oedipus and the Sphinx (Attic red-figure cup by the Oedipus painter)
artworks.description: Interior of Attic red-figure cup, ca. 470 B.C. Oedipus, dressed as a traveler, ponders the riddle of the Sphinx, who sits on an Ionic column. The Sphinx is winged, with a woman's head and a lion's body and tail.

artworks.name: Oedipus and the Sphinx by Gustave Moreau
artworks.description: Oil on canvas, 1864. The sphinx clutches Oedipus, ready to tear him in pieces, while Oedipus gazes at her intensely. Set in the mountains outside Thebes; includes a column with a serpent and an ancient vase with griffins' heads.

artworks.name: Darius painter's vase
artworks.description: Shows the violence of Laius and the dismay of Pelops and Chrysippus.

artworks.name: Capaneus vase
artworks.description: Campanian red-figure vase, ca. 350 B.C., depicting Capaneus climbing a ladder with torch and axe, with thunderbolt above.

artworks.name: Etruscan funerary ash urn (Death of Eteocles and Polynices)
artworks.description: Etruscan funerary ash urn (third to second century B.C.) depicting the fallen heroes with two supporters on each side and a winged female demon Vanth holding a torch.

artworks.name: Lucanian nestoris by the Dolon painter (Antigone Is Brought before Creon)
artworks.description: Lucanian (South Italian) nestoris by the Dolon painter, ca. 380 B.C., showing Antigone brought before Creon, who is seated on a stool wearing a tiara and oriental headdress, with two guards escorting her.

artworks.name: Apulian red-figure krater by the Darius painter
artworks.description: Krater depicting a scene from Sophocles' lost tragedy Thyestes at Sicyon, showing Adrastus, Thyestes, Pelopia, and other figures.

artworks.name: Death of Agamemnon krater
artworks.description: Attic red-figure krater by the Dokimasia painter, ca. 470 B.C., showing Aegisthus holding Agamemnon by the hair while Clytemnestra runs in with an axe.

artworks.name: Apulian red-figure krater
artworks.description: Ca. 370 B.C., showing Orestes clinging to the omphalos in the temple of Apollo, with Apollo warding off a Fury.

artworks.name: Electra at the Tomb of Agamemnon
artworks.description: Lucanian pelike by the Choephori painter, ca. 350 B.C., depicting Electra mourning at Agamemnon's tomb with Orestes and Hermes.

artworks.name: The Death of Aegisthus
artworks.description: Athenian krater by the Dokimasia painter, ca. 470 B.C. Depicts Orestes killing Aegisthus while Clytemnestra approaches with an axe and Electra runs in.

artworks.name: The Judgment of Paris by Lucas Cranach the Elder
artworks.description: Oil on panel, ca. 1528; depicts Paris as a corpulent knight, Hermes aged, and the three goddesses; Cupid draws bow; towers of Troy in background.

artworks.name: The Judgment of Paris mosaic from Antioch
artworks.description: Mosaic from Antioch, early second century A.D.; depicts Paris, Hermes, Hera, Athena, Aphrodite, Psyche, Cupid, and various animals.

artworks.name: The Death of Sarpedon
artworks.description: Athenian red-figure krater by Euphronios, ca. 510 B.C.; shows Hypnos and Thanatos carrying Sarpedon's body under Hermes' guidance.

artworks.name: Diomedes and Odysseus Stealing the Palladium from Troy
artworks.description: Detail from an Attic red-figure amphora by the Tyszkiewicz painter, early fifth century B.C.; Diomedes holds the Palladium.

artworks.name: Achilles and Ajax Playing a Board Game
artworks.description: Attic amphora signed by Exekias, ca. 535 B.C.; shows Achilles and Ajax playing a board game, partly armed.

artworks.name: Peleus Wrestles with Thetis
artworks.description: Red figure kylix by the Peithinos painter, ca. 510 B.C. Depicts Peleus holding Thetis as she transforms into a lion and snakes.

artworks.name: The Anger of Achilles
artworks.description: Oil on canvas by J.-L. David, 1819. Shows Achilles drawing his sword in anger at Agamemnon at Aulis, with Iphigenia and Clytemnestra.

artworks.name: Philoctetes on Lemnos
artworks.description: Red-figure lekythos, ca. 430 B.C. Depicts Philoctetes sitting alone on Lemnos with his bandaged foot and the bow of Heracles.

artworks.name: Hector and Andromache by Giorgio de Chirico
artworks.description: Oil on canvas, 1917, 35.5 x 23.5 in. Depicts Hector and Andromache as mannequins in a stagelike setting, with baby Astyanax as a steel wedge.

artworks.name: Priam and Achilles (red-figure skyphos by Brygos painter)
artworks.description: Red-figure skyphos depicting Priam approaching Achilles with gifts; Hector's body under couch.

artworks.name: The Death of Hector (modello by Peter Paul Rubens)
artworks.description: Modello for tapestry showing Achilles killing Hector, with Athena, shield, and river Scamander.

artworks.name: The Funeral of Patroclus (Apulian red-figure krater by Darius painter)
artworks.description: Krater showing pyre, Achilles killing Trojan prisoners, and Automedon dragging Hector's corpse.

artworks.name: The Building of the Trojan Horse
artworks.description: Oil on canvas by Giovanni Domenico Tiepolo, 1773, depicting the construction of the wooden horse with Epeus and Odysseus.

artworks.name: The Sack of Troy
artworks.description: Attic red-figure hydria by the Kleophrades painter, ca. 480 B.C., showing scenes of the sack including Priam, Astyanax, Neoptolemus, Aeneas, and Ajax Oïleus.

artworks.name: The Flight of Aeneas from Troy
artworks.description: Oil on canvas by Federico Barocci, 1598, depicting Aeneas, Ascanius, and Anchises fleeing Troy.

artworks.name: Flight from Troy
artworks.description: Marble statue by Gian-Lorenzo Bernini (1618-1619), height 86.5 in. Depicts Aeneas carrying Anchises, with the household gods; Ascanius not shown in detail.

artworks.name: François Vase
artworks.description: Attic black-figure krater by potter Ergotimos and painter Kleitias, ca. 575 B.C., height 30 in. Depicts multiple mythological scenes including the Calydonian boar hunt, chariot race of Patroclus' funeral games, wedding of Peleus and Thetis, and Achilles pursuing Troilus.

artworks.name: Calypso and Ulysses by Emily Marshall
artworks.description: Watercolor on paper, 1820–1835; 19 × 24 in. Calypso, in early 19th-century dress, tries to comfort Odysseus as he looks over the ocean thinking of Penelope. River landscape with palm tree.

artworks.name: The Blinding of Polyphemus
artworks.description: Proto-Attic vase from Eleusis, mid-7th century B.C.; height 56 in., neck 15 in. Odysseus (white) and companions drive pole into Cyclops' eye; he holds wine cup.

artworks.name: Odysseus Threatens Circe
artworks.description: Attic red-figure kalyx krater by the Persephone painter, 440 B.C. Depicts Circe fleeing from Odysseus, who threatens her with a sword; two transformed men approach.

artworks.name: Odysseus and the Sirens
artworks.description: Athenian red-figure stamnos, ca. 450 B.C. Odysseus lashed to the mast hears the Sirens' song; his men row with ears plugged; three Sirens on cliffs.

artworks.name: Odysseus and Nausicaä
artworks.description: Red-figure amphora, ca. 440 B.C. Odysseus holds olive branches as a suppliant; Athena stands between him and Nausicaä; clothes hang on a tree.

artworks.name: Penelope and the Suitors
artworks.description: Fresco by Pinturicchio, later transferred to canvas, depicting Penelope at her loom with Euryclea, Telemachus running to greet her, and Odysseus disguised as a beggar entering. Background shows the ship of the Phaeacians, Odysseus' boat shattered by Poseidon, and Odysseus meeting Circe.

artworks.name: The Return of Odysseus (Homage to Pintoricchio and Benin)
artworks.description: Watercolor, gouache, and ink on paper by Romare Bearden (1977), part of the Black Odyssey series. Depicts the same scene as Pinturicchio's fresco with black figures, referencing African art.

artworks.name: The Washing of Odysseus' Feet
artworks.description: Attic red-figure skyphos, ca. 440 B.C., depicting Euryclea recognizing Odysseus by his scar, with Penelope at her loom on the other side.

artworks.name: Danaë and the Brazen Tower
artworks.description: Oil on canvas by Edward Burne-Jones (1888), depicting Danaë watching the raising of her prison.

artworks.name: Medusa
artworks.description: Oil on wooden shield by Caravaggio (ca. 1598), depicting Medusa after decapitation.

artworks.name: Danaë and the Chest
artworks.description: Attic red-figure lekythos (ca. 470 B.C.), showing Danaë and infant Perseus in chest with Acrisius.

artworks.name: Perseus Beheads Medusa
artworks.description: Limestone metope from Selinus, ca. 540 B.C., height 58 in. Shows Athena, Perseus, and Pegasus springing from Medusa's body.

artworks.name: Perseus and Andromeda
artworks.description: Oil on canvas by Titian, 1554–1556, 70½ × 77¾ in. Depicts Perseus with winged sandals and harpe.

artworks.name: Perseus Attacks the Sea-Monster
artworks.description: Etruscan black-figure hydria from Caere, ca. 530 B.C., height 15¾ in. Shows Perseus with rock and scimitar.

artworks.name: Perseus
artworks.description: Bronze sculpture by Benvenuto Cellini, 1545–1553, in Loggia dei Lanzi, Florence. Perseus holds Medusa's head.

artworks.name: The Baleful Head
artworks.description: Oil on canvas by Edward Burne-Jones, 1887, 60½ × 50¾ in. Part of Perseus cycle; shows Perseus and Andromeda looking at Medusa's reflection.

artworks.name: Bellerophon and the Chimera (Byzantine ivory plaque)
artworks.description: Byzantine ivory plaque, fifth century; 8 ½ × 3 ½ in. Bellerophon rides on Pegasus to the right and thrusts his lance into the lion's mouth, as the monster collapses on its front paws. Its serpent-tail twines round one of three trees, and the goat's head melds with another.

artworks.name: Metopes of the temple of Zeus at Olympia
artworks.description: Metopes depicting the Twelve Labors of Heracles on the temple of Zeus at Olympia.

artworks.name: Hercules and the Lernaean Hydra
artworks.description: Oil on canvas by Gustave Moreau (1875/76), depicting Hercules with lionskin, bow, and club fighting the seven-headed Hydra.

artworks.name: Heracles, Assisted by Athena, Cleans the Augean Stables
artworks.description: Marble metope from the east porch of the Temple of Zeus at Olympia, ca. 460 B.C., showing Athena directing Heracles with a crowbar.

artworks.name: Athena, Heracles, and Atlas
artworks.description: Metope no. 10 from the Temple of Zeus at Olympia, ca. 460 B.C., showing Atlas returning with the apples while Heracles holds up the sky with Athena's help.

artworks.name: Heracles Shows Cerberus to Eurystheus
artworks.description: Etruscan hydria from Caere, ca. 530 B.C.; depicts Heracles presenting Cerberus to a terrified Eurystheus leaping into a jar.

artworks.name: Hylas and the Nymphs
artworks.description: Oil on canvas by J. W. Waterhouse (1896); shows Hylas being lured by seven water-nymphs.

artworks.name: Nessus and Deïanira by Guido Reni
artworks.description: Oil on canvas, 1623, depicting the centaur Nessus carrying off Deïanira while Heracles takes an arrow from his quiver.

artworks.name: Heracles and Apollo Struggle for the Pythian Tripod (Attic red-figure amphora)
artworks.description: Attic red-figure amphora by the Andocides painter, ca. 520 B.C., showing Athena watching Heracles and Apollo struggling for the tripod.

artworks.name: The Death of Nessus (Attic black-figure amphora)
artworks.description: Attic black-figure amphora, ca. 620 B.C., depicting Heracles killing Nessus with a sword.

artworks.name: The Apotheosis of Hercules by Peter Paul Rubens
artworks.description: Oil on panel, 1636, showing Hercules ascending from the pyre to Olympus on a chariot.

artworks.name: The Choice of Heracles by Annibale Carracci
artworks.description: Oil on canvas, 1596, depicting Heracles choosing between Pleasure and Virtue.

artworks.name: Farnese Hercules
artworks.description: Marble copy by Glycon of an original by Lysippus, found in the Baths of Caracalla, showing Heracles leaning on his club with lionskin draped over a stump.

artworks.name: Hercules Victor (The Farnese Hercules) by Hendrik Goltzius
artworks.description: Engraving showing Heracles from the rear, clutching the Apples of the Hesperides, with Latin iambic lines describing his labors.

artworks.name: The Discovery of the Infant Erichthonius
artworks.description: Oil on canvas by Peter Paul Rubens, ca. 1616. Depicts Aglauros opening the basket containing Erichthonius and showing him to her sisters Pandrosos and Herse. Cupid gestures, background includes fountain of Artemis and herm of Pan.

artworks.name: Cephalus and Aurora
artworks.description: Oil on canvas by Nicolas Poussin, ca. 1630. Cephalus gazes at portrait of Procris held by cupid, resisting Aurora. Background shows Pegasus and river-god.

artworks.name: The Banquet of Tereus
artworks.description: Oil on canvas by Peter Paul Rubens (1577–1640), 1636–1638, 77 × 105 in. Depicts Procne showing the head of Itys to Tereus, with Philomela behind her.

artworks.name: The Labors of Theseus (Attic red-figure kylix)
artworks.description: Attic red-figure kylix, ca. 475 B.C., height 5 in., diameter 12¾ in. Depicts the cycle of Theseus' labors on both exterior and interior; interior shows Theseus dragging the Minotaur.

artworks.name: Theseus and Amphitrite
artworks.description: Attic red-figure cup by the painter Onesimos and signed by the potter Euphronios, ca. 500 B.C.; diameter 15¾ in. Depicts Theseus held up underwater by a Triton, with Amphitrite holding a wreath and Athena looking on.

artworks.name: Death of a Monster
artworks.description: Pencil on paper by Pablo Picasso, 1937, 15 × 22¼ in. Depicts a dying Minotaur seeing itself in a mirror held by a sea-goddess.

artworks.name: Dionysus and Ariadne
artworks.description: Marble sarcophagus, ca. A.D. 180; width 77 in., height (without lid) 20½ in., height of lid 11 in. Shows Dionysus approaching Ariadne on a chariot drawn by a centaur, with various figures including Pan, silenus, cupids, maenads, and Pentheus.

artworks.name: Derveni Krater
artworks.description: Bronze krater from the second half of the fourth century BC, height 35.5 in, discovered at Derveni in 1962. Reliefs show Dionysus seated with Ariadne, a panther, birds, animals, vines, ivy, maenads, and handles in the form of serpents framing a horned god and Heracles.

artworks.name: The Fall of Icarus by Pieter Brueghel the Elder
artworks.description: Oil on canvas, 30 x 44 in. Depicts Icarus' legs visible in the sea near a galleon, with a ploughman, fisherman, and shepherd, and a partridge (perdix) referencing Perdix.

artworks.name: Icarus by Henri Matisse
artworks.description: Stencil print of a paper cutout, 1947, 16.5 x 25.5 in, from Matisse's Jazz. Shows a black silhouette of Icarus with a red heart against sky and stars.

artworks.name: The Building of the Argo
artworks.description: Terra-cotta relief from Campania, mid-first century A.D., showing Athena helping a workman place a sail, and Argus working on the stern.

artworks.name: Jason Is Disgorged by the Dragon That Guards the Golden Fleece
artworks.description: Athenian red-figure cup by Douris, ca. 470 B.C.; diameter 11 ¾ in. Depicts Athena watching the bearded dragon disgorge Jason; the fleece hangs on a tree.

artworks.name: Jason Takes the Golden Fleece
artworks.description: Oil on panel by Peter Paul Rubens (1577–1640), 1636, 10 ½ × 11 ¼ in. Jason passes by a statue of Mars with the fleece draped over his left arm, dressed as a Roman soldier.

artworks.name: Medea by Eduardo Paolozzi
artworks.description: Welded aluminum sculpture from 1964, height 81 in., depicting Medea with machine parts, implying destructive power.

artworks.name: Medea Leaves Corinth in a Chariot Drawn by Dragons
artworks.description: Lucanian Calyx-Krater, c. 400 B.C., red-figure earthenware, showing Medea in a chariot sent by the Sun, with Furies, Jason, and mourners.

artworks.name: Medea Murders Her Son
artworks.description: Campanian red-figure amphora by the Ixion painter, ca. 325 B.C. Depicts Medea thrusting a sword into her son's body, set in a temple with a statue of a god.
